questions.q: What is a primary characteristic of a physical change?
a: No new chemical substances are formed, and it is usually reversible
A completely new substance is always created

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
What happens during a chemical reaction?
a: Reactants rearrange their bonds to form new products with different properties
Molecules move apart without changing structure

questions.q: Which observation strongly indicates that a chemical change has taken place?
a: A permanent color change, fizzing, or release of light and heat occurs

questions.q: Why is dissolving salt in water classified as a physical change?
a: The salt can be recovered by evaporating the water
Water changes into hydrogen and oxygen

questions.q: Which process represents a reversible physical change?
a: Boiling liquid water into steam and condensing it back

questions.q: What occurs when magnesium ribbon is burned strongly in oxygen gas?
a: A chemical reaction takes place, producing white magnesium oxide powder

questions.q: Which of the following changes is generally irreversible?
a: Cooking raw meat or boiling an egg

questions.q: When iron rusts, what is the chemical nature of the rust compared to pure iron?
a: Rust is a brand new chemical substance (iron oxide) with different properties
Rust has the exact same chemical makeup

questions.q: Which everyday activity is an example of a physical change?
In a chemical reaction, what are the starting substances called?
What term describes a chemical reaction that releases heat to its surroundings?
Why is the melting of wax considered a physical change?
a: The liquid wax can solidify again upon cooling, and no new substance is created

questions.q: Which of the following is evidence that a chemical reaction has produced a gas?
a: Bubbles of effervescence or fizzing are observed
The liquid volume increases without adding anything

questions.q: What is formed when an acid reacts with an alkali?
Mixing baking soda and vinegar causes bubbling due to the release of which gas?
What happens to total mass during physical and chemical changes?
a: Total mass is conserved in both physical and chemical changes
Mass is destroyed during chemical changes
Mass increases significantly during physical changes

questions.q: Which change involves thermal decomposition using heat?
a: Heating green copper carbonate powder until it turns black and releases gas

questions.q: What happens to chemical bonds during a chemical change?
a: Existing bonds break and new bonds form to create products

questions.q: Which indicator represents a physical change rather than a chemical reaction?
a: Change of state like melting or freezing

questions.q: Which of the following is a sign of a chemical change?
Is evaporating water a physical or chemical change?
What is the term for a chemical reaction that absorbs heat from its surroundings, causing the temperature to drop?
Which of these represents a chemical change in the kitchen?
When wood burns, what are the primary products formed?
a: Ash, carbon dioxide, and water vapor

questions.q: Which property can be used to easily separate iron from a physical mixture with sand?
Why is chopping a carrot considered a physical change?
a: It creates a new chemical compound
It changes size and shape, but the carrot material remains chemically identical

questions.q: What term describes the new substances formed at the end of a chemical reaction?
Which of these changes is reversible?
a: Freezing liquid juice into an ice lolly

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT typically a sign of a chemical reaction?
a: A change of state from solid to liquid

questions.q: What happens when anhydrous copper sulfate powder is mixed with water?
a: It turns green and produces gas
It undergoes a chemical reaction turning blue and releasing heat

questions.q: Which statement best describes atoms in a chemical change?
a: Atoms are rearranged to form new combinations
